# Stellend

> Turkish lira in and out of a Stellar lending pool, non-custodially. Borrowers lock a
> Soroban asset and borrow USDC from a Blend v2 pool, and the anchor pays TRY to their
> IBAN. Lenders send TRY by bank transfer, which the anchor converts to USDC and supplies
> to the same pool. Stellar TESTNET proof of concept only: mock TRY anchor, Blend testnet
> pool, never mainnet.

## Start here

- [Live app](https://stellend-jow5cyrhg-medine1729s-projects.vercel.app/dashboard): testnet deployment (per-deployment Vercel URL; also https://stellend-cyan.vercel.app)
- [Live status and deployed ids (JSON)](/api/health): commit, dependency checks, contract ids
- [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/medine2906/stellend_/blob/main/AGENTS.md): rules for working in this repo, commands, definition of done
- [README](https://github.com/medine2906/stellend_/blob/main/README.md): product, flows, limits, deployed artifacts
- [Docs index](https://github.com/medine2906/stellend_/blob/main/docs/README.md): architecture, API, data model, PRD

## Facts that do not change

- No server-held keys: the server prepares unsigned XDR, the user's wallet signs, the server verifies and submits.
- The chain is authoritative; Supabase is a cache (except the borrow intent row).
- Amounts and identity never come from the client: identity from the SEP-10 session, amounts from the server's reserved intent.
- The advance registry (our Soroban contract) is optional, has no admin key, and is never a gate.
- `due_at` is a signed target date, not an enforced deadline; a Blend position is perpetual, not a term loan.
- Standards used: SEP-10, SEP-6, SEP-38. SEP-12 KYC is deliberately not implemented.
